one_liner: DealCloud has a broad REST API and an official MCP server, but API access requires permissions within a DealCloud organisation.

auth.notes: The REST API uses an API key to obtain an OAuth2 bearer token through the client-credentials flow. DealCloud also documents authorized user proxying; MCP separately supports user sign-in through OAuth 2.0.

access.notes: API capability must be enabled for a user group within a DealCloud site. No self-serve route to a site or credentials for a non-customer was established.

api.notes: The documentation covers multiple functional areas and authorized requests on behalf of users.

mcp.notes: DealCloud documents a default server and optional write tools. The MCP feature requires the DealCloud with Celeste license.

verdict.rationale: DealCloud documents a broad REST API and authorized per-user requests, but API capability must be enabled within a DealCloud organisation. A self-serve path to credentials for a non-customer was not established.

evidence.quote: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token, which is then used in the HTTP Authentication header for API requests.
Once user permissions are set, click the User icon at the top-right of your DealCloud screen and select Profile. Scroll down to the API Key section and click Enable.
DealCloud MCP uses OAuth to authenticate, letting AI assistants connect on behalf of an individual user.

To enable API access, ensure the intended user is assigned to a user group with the appropriate permissions. Navigate to Admin > User Management, select the relevant user group, go to Capabilities > Site Areas, and enable "API".
If you do not see the Admin section, contact your organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager (CSM) for assistance.
Data stored in the dedicated cloud (hosted in Microsoft Azure) is protected by Azure’s comprehensive security framework, which includes advanced encryption and access controls.
This site provides a comprehensive overview of our REST APIs, their capabilities, and available endpoints.
Our APIs are organized into functional areas. Each area includes multiple endpoints designed to help you perform specific tasks related to that category.
Once completed, proxy requests are serviced as if they were made by the principal user, consequently respecting their capabilities, permissions, data access, and auditability.
DealCloud provides a default MCP Server out-of-the-box without any configuration required. It exposes your site's full schema and is the fastest way to get connected.
To let assistants create and update records, go to Tools > MCP Servers, edit the MCP Server, and turn on the Enable Write Tools toggle.
This feature is available as part of the DealCloud with Celeste license.
Principal and proxy users, both, need to have the API capability enabled in User Management.
If you cannot enable or copy your API key, verify your user group permissions and contact your admin or DealCloud support.

problems: The Composio toolkit URL would not load; the memo reports an absent catalog match but supplies no quoted evidence for that finding, so catalog status is unknown.
No official statement ties REST API credentials to a free account, trial or purchasable plan. A non-customer’s route to obtaining a DealCloud site remains unresolved.
The API release note describes MCP read access, while current MCP documentation describes optional write tools.
name: DealCloud

verification.note: Quotes show OAuth2 client-credentials bearer tokens, a user-enabled API key, and MCP OAuth. They do not explicitly say the API key is exchanged for that token, but nothing recommends a different primary method.

Enabling API requires a user-group capability set in Admin > User Management, and non-admins are told to contact their organization admin or CSM. The note that no non-customer self-serve route exists is an absence inference, not a quoted denial.
Public docs describe a REST API organized into functional areas with multiple endpoints and user-proxy requests. Nothing contradicts breadth broad.

Vendor docs describe a default MCP server usable out of the box plus an optional write-tools toggle, so official and generally available hold. The Celeste-license sentence does not name MCP, but it does not label the server beta or unlaunched.
No claim was made, so there is nothing to check.
A documented REST API plus credentials that an existing organization's admin must enable is buildable with an admin-approval caveat, not a sales or partnership block.
